mainTopic: מזוזה: the gates of the מקדש, city gates, the danger at מחוזא, and which buildings are exempt
overview: This amud finishes a ברייתא saying that only שער ניקנור had a מזוזה, because it led into לשכת פרהדרין. The גמרא shows this can fit even רבי יהודה, because the chamber and its gate were one single גזירה. A ברייתא then teaches that city gates also need a מזוזה. אביי asks why the gates of מחוזא had none and concludes that it was because of סכנה, since public מזוזות drew dangerous attention from the authorities. The rule that שלוחי מצוה are not harmed does not apply where danger is constant, as we see from שמואל. Next, רב כהנא and רב יהודה argue over a ברייתא exempting barns and storehouses because women are 'נאותות' there. רב כהנא says the word means bathing, and רב יהודה says it means adorning. Each reads the longer ברייתא to fit his view. The amud ends with a ברייתא that seems to contradict רב יהודה, and the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Only שער ניקנור had a מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא states that among the eastern gates of the עזרה, only שער ניקנור had a מזוזה, because it led into לשכת פרהדרין.
steps.simpleTranslation: All the gates there had no מזוזה, except שער ניקנור, because just inside it was לשכת פרהדרין.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a ברייתא about which gates of the מקדש had a מזוזה. Only one gate did, and the ברייתא gives the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Gates of the מקדש normally do not need a מזוזה, because they are not entrances to a home. שער ניקנור was different because it led into לשכת פרהדרין, which did have a מזוזה. The gate's obligation comes from the room it leads into.

keyTerms.meaning: The Nikanor Gate, a main gate of the עזרה (Temple courtyard)
The chamber where the כהן גדול stayed for seven days before יום כיפור
Parchment with Torah passages affixed to a doorpost

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a gate can need a מזוזה because of the room it leads into. The next steps question exactly this.

phrases.english: All the gates that were there
did not have a mezuzah,
except for the Nikanor Gate,
for inside it was the Chamber of Parhedrin.
phrases.notes: Since the chamber had a מזוזה, so did the gate leading to it.

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל הַשְּׁעָרִים שֶׁהָיוּ שָׁם לֹא הָיָה לָהֶם מְזוּזָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun earlier on the daf about מזוזה in the מקדש.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only שער ניקנור had a מזוזה, because it led into לשכת פרהדרין.

steps.title: Can this ברייתא follow רבי יהודה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the ברייתא follows the רבנן, because for רבי יהודה the gate's מזוזה would be a גזירה built on another גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this ברייתא follows the רבנן and not רבי יהודה? If it followed רבי יהודה, the chamber's own מזוזה is only a גזירה. Would we then make a second גזירה to protect the first one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to identify whose opinion the ברייתא follows. It argues that the ברייתא cannot match רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier on the daf, the רבנן hold that לשכת פרהדרין needs a מזוזה מדאורייתא, so a rabbinic מזוזה on its gate is a normal safeguard. רבי יהודה holds the chamber's מזוזה is itself only rabbinic. A מזוזה on the gate would then be a decree protecting a decree, which חז״ל normally do not make.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion the גמרא may reject)
A decree to protect another decree, which is normally not made

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase "הִיא גּוּפַהּ גְּזֵירָה" refers to the chamber's מזוזה, not the gate's. For רבי יהודה the chamber itself is already only rabbinic.

phrases.english: Shall we say it is the Rabbis
and not Rabbi Yehuda?
For if it were Rabbi Yehuda,
it itself (the chamber's mezuzah) is a decree,
phrases.notes: For רבי יהודה, the chamber is obligated only rabbinically.

phrases.english: and shall we then go and decree
a decree for a decree?

steps.triggerLanguage: לֵימָא רַבָּנַן הִיא וְלָא רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Analyzes the ברייתא of step 1 to find whose opinion it follows.
steps.kashyaTarget: Matching the ברייתא with רבי יהודה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: For רבי יהודה, the gate's מזוזה would be a decree protecting a decree, which is normally not done.

steps.title: It was all one decree
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא can follow רבי יהודה, because the chamber and its gate were included in one single גזירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say it follows רבי יהודה. The whole thing is one single גזירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the problem and keeps the ברייתא as a possible match for רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There was no second decree layered on the first. When חז״ל decreed a מזוזה for the chamber, they decreed it for the chamber and its gate together, in one act. So the rule against "גזירה לגזירה" does not apply.

keyTerms.meaning: All of it, the entire thing

steps.whatToRemember: A rabbinic decree can cover several things at once. That is not the same as a decree built on top of a decree.

phrases.english: You can even say it is Rabbi Yehuda;
the whole thing is one single decree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem raised in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing: two layers are shown to be one decree
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The gate's מזוזה would be a separate, second decree protecting the chamber's decree.
steps.terutzMaskana: The chamber and the gate were decreed together, so the ברייתא can follow רבי יהודה too.

steps.title: All kinds of gates need a מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from "בשעריך" that the gates of houses, courtyards, provinces and towns all need a מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: "בשעריך" (your gates) includes the gates of houses, courtyards, provinces and towns. All of them need a מזוזה, as it says "and write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates."
steps.whatsHappening: Since the topic is מזוזה, the גמרא now brings a ברייתא about which gates need one. This opens a new discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "בשעריך" in the פסוק widens the מצוה beyond the door of a house. It also includes courtyard gates and even the gates of whole cities. This sets up the next question about the city gates of מחוזא.

keyTerms.meaning: On your gates (from the פסוק of מזוזה)

steps.whyThisMatters: City gates are obligated in מזוזה, as is brought down in הלכה. This ברייתא is the source.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: "On your gates" —
both the gates of houses,
and the gates of courtyards,
and the gates of provinces,
and the gates of towns,
have the obligation of the מצוה in that place,
because it is stated:
"And you shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from מזוזה in the מקדש to the general laws of מזוזה on gates.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Gates of houses, courtyards, provinces and towns all need a מזוזה, learned from "בשעריך".

steps.title: Why do the gates of מחוזא have no מזוזה?
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks רב ספרא why the רבנן did not put a מזוזה on the city gates of מחוזא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב ספרא: Those gates of מחוזא, why didn't the רבנן put a מזוזה on them?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי applies the ברייתא to a real place. מחוזא's gates seem to need a מזוזה, yet they have none.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to the ברייתא, city gates need a מזוזה. מחוזא was a city with a Jewish majority, so it should have one. אביי wants to know why it is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: מחוזא, a Jewish city in Bavel

phrases.english: Abaye said to Rav Safra:
Those gates of Mechoza,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא עֲבַדוּ לְהוּ רַבָּנַן מְזוּזָה?
phrases.english: what is the reason the Sages did not make a mezuzah for them?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי אֲבוּלֵּי דְמָחוֹזָא מַאי טַעְמָא לָא עֲבַדוּ לְהוּ רַבָּנַן מְזוּזָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא of step 4 to an actual case that seems to contradict it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the city gates of מחוזא lack a מזוזה, despite the ברייתא.

steps.title: They are part of the fortress
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא answers that those gates are not real city gates. They are built as support for the fortress of turrets.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Those gates were made as reinforcement for the fortress of turrets.
steps.whatsHappening: רב ספרא explains that these gates are not city gates. They are part of a military fortress, so the ברייתא does not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The gates are classified as part of the fortress structure, not as entrances to the city. A fortress is not a place where people live, so it seems to need no מזוזה. This is the point אביי will challenge next.

phrases.english: He said to him: Those are reinforcement
for the fortress of turrets; that is what they were made for.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנְהוּ חִזּוּק לְאַקְרָא דְכוּבֵי הוּא דַּעֲבִידִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers אביי's question in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The gates belong to the fortress, not the city, so the city-gate obligation does not apply.

steps.title: The fortress itself should need a מזוזה
steps.stepSummary: אביי pushes back: the fortress itself should need a מזוזה, because the prison guard lives there.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The fortress itself should need a מזוזה, since there is a living space there for the prison guard.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב ספרא's answer. Calling the gates part of the fortress does not solve the problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ספרא assumed a fortress needs no מזוזה. אביי points out that someone lives there, the guard of the prison. A building with a residence in it should need a מזוזה, so the gates should still have one.

phrases.english: He said to him: But the fortress of turrets itself
should require a mezuzah,
since there is a dwelling in it
for the guard of the prison,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב ספרא's answer in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב ספרא's claim that the gates are exempt because they belong to the fortress
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The fortress has a residence for the prison guard, so it should itself need a מזוזה.

steps.title: Proof from a בית הכנסת with a home for the חזן
steps.stepSummary: אביי proves his point from a ברייתא: a בית הכנסת with a home for the חזן needs a מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: a בית הכנסת that has a living space for the חזן הכנסת needs a מזוזה!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי backs up his challenge with a ברייתא. One person living there is enough to obligate the building.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית הכנסת on its own needs no מזוזה, because it is not a home. Once the חזן lives there, it becomes obligated. The same logic should obligate a fortress where the prison guard lives.

keyTerms.meaning: For it was taught (brings a ברייתא as proof)

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets a general principle: a building used for public purposes needs a מזוזה once someone lives in it.

phrases.english: for it was taught:
A synagogue that has in it
a dwelling for the synagogue attendant
is obligated in mezuzah!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּהָא תַּנְיָא: בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ בֵּית דִּירָה לְחַזַּן הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the challenge of step 7 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That a fortress with a guard's residence needs a מזוזה
steps.raayaSupportSource: ברייתא: a בית הכנסת with a residence for the חזן is obligated in מזוזה

steps.title: אביי's new answer: the gates had no מזוזה because of danger
steps.stepSummary: אביי drops the earlier explanation and says the gates of מחוזא had no מזוזה because of סכנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי said: the reason is danger.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a brand-new answer to his own original question about why the city gates of מחוזא had no מזוזה. The reason is danger.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier answer said the gates were not real city gates. אביי himself attacked that answer, because the fortress should still need a מזוזה. So he now agrees the gates really need a מזוזה. The reason none was put up is that putting one up was dangerous.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather. It signals that the earlier answer is dropped and a new one is given.

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not saying these gates are outside the obligation of מזוזה. They really are obligated. Danger is simply what prevented putting one up.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that a real obligation can be set aside in practice when carrying it out puts people in danger.

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye said:
It is because of danger.
phrases.notes: The danger was that the non-Jews of the city could treat a מזוזה as suspicious.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the proof in step 8 knocked down רב ספרא's answer, אביי offers a new reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason that replaces the earlier one
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The gates had no מזוזה because they were not true city gates.
steps.terutzMaskana: The gates were obligated, but a מזוזה was not put up because of danger.

steps.title: Proof that public מזוזות were dangerous to check
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says a public מזוזה is checked very rarely. רבי יהודה tells of an inspector in צפורי who was fined a thousand זוז for checking מזוזות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: a private מזוזה is checked twice in seven years, and a public one twice in fifty years. And רבי יהודה said: there was a story about an inspector who was checking מזוזות in the upper market of צפורי. An official caught him and took a thousand זוז from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up אביי's 'danger' answer. It brings a ברייתא and a story showing that public מזוזות drew dangerous attention.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Public מזוזות are checked far less often than private ones. The story shows the risk: a man checking public מזוזות was caught by a government official and heavily fined. So a public מזוזה on a city gate could invite danger.

keyTerms.meaning: An individual (here, a privately owned מזוזה)
The public (here, a publicly owned מזוזה)
Here it means a seven-year cycle, not a week

steps.confusionAlert: 'בשבוע' here does NOT mean twice a week. It means twice in a seven-year cycle (a שמיטה cycle), just as 'ביובל' means twice in fifty years.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraita: an individual's mezuzah
is checked twice in a seven-year cycle,
phrases.notes: It is checked to see if it was stolen or became unfit.

phrases.english: and a public one, twice in a Jubilee (fifty years).
And Rabbi Yehuda said:
There was an incident with a certain inspector
who was checking mezuzot
in the upper marketplace of Tzippori,
and a certain official found him
and took a thousand zuz from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports אביי's claim of danger.
steps.raayaObject: That a public מזוזה posed a real danger
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about how often מזוזות are checked, plus רבי יהודה's story from צפורי

steps.title: But people doing a מצוה are not harmed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: רבי אלעזר said שלוחי מצוה are not harmed, so how could checking מזוזות be dangerous?
steps.simpleTranslation: But did not רבי אלעזר say: people on the way to do a מצוה are not harmed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea of danger. It quotes רבי אלעזר's rule that someone doing a מצוה is protected from harm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If doing a מצוה protects a person, the inspector should not have been harmed. Putting a מזוזה on the city gate should not be dangerous either. This seems to undercut the 'danger' reason.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't (someone) say? This introduces a challenge.
People on the way to do a מצוה

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Elazar say:
those on a מצוה mission are not harmed?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'danger' reason given in steps 9-10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that doing the מצוה of מזוזה was dangerous
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שלוחי מצוה are protected, so the danger should not exist.

steps.title: Where danger is constant, it is different
steps.stepSummary: Where harm is likely and ongoing, the protection does not apply. Even שמואל worried about שאול and was told to bring a cover story.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where the danger is constant, it is different. As it is written: 'And שמואל said: How can I go? שאול will hear and kill me. And ה׳ said: Take a calf with you and say, I have come to offer a sacrifice to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The protection for people doing a מצוה does not cover a situation where danger is fixed and expected.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר's rule covers ordinary, unexpected risks. When danger is clear and constant, one may not rely on it. The proof is from שמואל: on a mission from ה׳ Himself, he still feared שאול, and ה׳ gave him a cover story instead of promising protection.

keyTerms.meaning: Where the harm is fixed or constant
A young calf (שמואל's cover for his trip)

steps.whatToRemember: The rule that שלוחי מצוה are not harmed does not apply where danger is constant. That is why a מזוזה on the gates of מחוזא could be left off because of סכנה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a lasting principle: one does not rely on a miracle when danger is clear, even while doing a מצוה.

phrases.english: Where the danger is constant, it is different.
As it is written: 'And Samuel said:
How can I go? Saul will hear and kill me.

phrases.aramaic: וַיֹּאמֶר ה׳ עֶגְלַת בָּקָר תִּקַּח בְּיָדֶךָ
phrases.english: And God said: Take a calf in your hand,
and say: I have come to offer a sacrifice to God.'
phrases.notes: Even on a mission from ה׳ Himself, a cover was needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from רבי אלעזר.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שלוחי מצוה are protected in every case.
steps.terutzMaskana: Where danger is constant and expected, the protection is not relied upon.

steps.title: Storage buildings are exempt because women 'make use' of them
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא teaches a ברייתא: hay sheds, cattle barns, woodsheds and storehouses are exempt from מזוזה because women are 'נאותות' in them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא taught before רב יהודה: a hay shed, a cattle barn, a woodshed and a storehouse are exempt from מזוזה, because women 'make use' of them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רב כהנא quotes a ברייתא listing buildings that are exempt from מזוזה, and the reason uses an unclear word, 'נאותות'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives a reason tied to what women do in these buildings. The rest of the section will argue about what 'נאותות' means and how it explains the exemption.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Make use of' or 'benefit from'. The exact meaning is debated next.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנֵי רַב כָּהֲנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana taught before Rav Yehuda:
A hay shed and a cattle barn
and a woodshed and a storehouse
are exempt from mezuzah,
because the women 'make use' of them.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנֵי רַב כָּהֲנָא קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic about which buildings are exempt from מזוזה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hay sheds, cattle barns, woodsheds and storehouses are exempt from מזוזה, because women are 'נאותות' in them.

steps.title: First explanation: 'make use' means bathe
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains 'נאותות' as 'רוחצות', meaning women bathe there.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what does 'נאותות' mean? They bathe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the unclear word means and answers that women bathe in these buildings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this reading, the exemption comes from modesty. A place where women bathe unclothed is not a fitting place for a מזוזה.

phrases.english: And what does 'make use' mean?
They bathe.
phrases.notes: A one-word answer. It stands alone because it is the full answer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the key word in the ברייתא of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Women bathe there, so a מזוזה does not belong there.

steps.title: רב יהודה: a plain cattle barn is exempt anyway
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה objects: if bathing is the reason, a normal barn would be obligated. Yet a ברייתא says a cattle barn is exempt in any case.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said to him: the reason is that they bathe there, so a plain one would be obligated? But a ברייתא teaches that a cattle barn is exempt from מזוזה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה challenges the 'bathing' explanation using another ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the exemption depends on bathing, a barn where no one bathes would need a מזוזה. But another ברייתא exempts a cattle barn with no conditions. So the exemption cannot depend on bathing.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said to him:
The reason is because they bathe,
so plain ones would be obligated?
phrases.notes: This is a דיוק, an inference from the stated reason.

phrases.english: But it was taught: a cattle barn
is exempt from mezuzah!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה טַעְמָא דְּרוֹחֲצוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'bathing' reading from step 14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading implies a plain barn is obligated, but another ברייתא exempts a plain barn.

steps.title: New explanation: 'make use' means adorn themselves
steps.stepSummary: 'נאותות' means women adorn themselves there. The ברייתא means: even though women adorn themselves there, these buildings are still exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'נאותות' mean? They adorn themselves. And this is what it teaches: even though women adorn themselves in them, they are exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה proposes a new reading. The word is reread as 'adorn themselves', and the reason becomes an 'even though'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the women's use is not the reason for the exemption. The point is that even a clean, nice room where women get dressed up is still exempt, because it is a storage building and not a home. This fits the ברייתא that a barn is exempt anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what it teaches

phrases.english: Rather: what does 'make use' mean? They adorn themselves.
And this is what it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַנָּשִׁים מִתְקַשְּׁטוֹת בָּהֶן, פְּטוּרִין.
phrases.english: Even though the women adorn themselves in them, they are exempt.
phrases.notes: 'מפני ש' (because) is reread as 'אף על פי ש' (even though).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the 'bathing' reading after the challenge in step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'נאותות' means bathing, and that is the reason for the exemption.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'נאותות' means adorning, and the buildings are exempt even though women adorn themselves there.

steps.title: רב כהנא: a barn where women adorn themselves is obligated
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא objects with a ברייתא: a cattle barn is exempt, but one where women adorn themselves is obligated in מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא said to him: buildings where women adorn themselves are exempt? But a ברייתא teaches: a cattle barn is exempt from מזוזה, and one where women adorn themselves is obligated in מזוזה!
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא challenges the new 'adorning' reading with a ברייתא that says the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new reading says women adorning themselves does not create an obligation. But this ברייתא says that when women adorn themselves in a barn, it becomes obligated. The two seem to contradict directly.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana said to him:
And ones where women adorn themselves are exempt?
But it was taught: a cattle barn
is exempt from mezuzah,
and one in which women adorn themselves
is obligated in mezuzah!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא וְשֶׁהַנָּשִׁים מִתְקַשְּׁטוֹת בָּהֶן פְּטוּרִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the 'adorning' reading from step 16.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that buildings where women adorn themselves are exempt
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא explicitly says a barn where women adorn themselves is obligated.

steps.title: רב כהנא: the plain barn is also a dispute between תנאים
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא answers רב יהודה's earlier challenge from step 15. רב יהודה will have to say the adorning case is a dispute between תנאים. In the same way, רב כהנא says the plain barn case is also a dispute between תנאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what do you have to say? That the case of places where women adorn themselves is a dispute between תנאים? For me too, the plain barn case is a dispute between תנאים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא answers the ברייתא that רב יהודה used against him in step 15. He points out that רב יהודה also has to explain away a ברייתא (step 17) as one side of a dispute between תנאים, and he says he can do the same.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה attacked the 'bathing' reading in step 15, because a ברייתא exempts a plain cattle barn. רב כהנא answers him: to escape my ברייתא (a barn where women adorn themselves is obligated), you will have to say it follows a different תנא. In the same way, I say the ברייתא exempting a plain barn follows one תנא, while other תנאים obligate it. The next step brings the proof.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, what do you have to say?
it is a dispute between תנאים

steps.confusionAlert: Be careful: 'סתמא' here does not mean 'anonymous'. It means a plain, ordinary barn where nothing special like adorning or bathing happens.

phrases.english: Rather, what do you have to say?
That the case of women adorning themselves is a dispute between Tannaim?
For me too, the plain case is a dispute between Tannaim.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רב כהנא answers רב יהודה's קשיא of step 15. He points out that after step 17, רב יהודה too must rely on a dispute between תנאים.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the contradiction to a dispute between תנאים
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא that exempts a plain cattle barn disproves רב כהנא's 'bathing' reading.
steps.terutzMaskana: Plain barns are subject to a dispute between תנאים, so רב כהנא's reading still stands.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows תנאים disagree about plain barns
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא brings a ברייתא proving that some exempt barns and storehouses from מזוזה while others obligate them.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: 'Your house' means your house that is set aside for you. This excludes a hay shed, a cattle barn, a woodshed and storehouses, which are exempt from מזוזה. And some obligate them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא brings a ברייתא to prove his claim. It shows that there is a real disagreement about whether barns need a מזוזה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא first exempts barns and storehouses, because the פסוק says 'your house', meaning a house used for living. It then adds 'יש מחייבין', meaning some obligate them. That second opinion proves that תנאים disagree about plain barns, just as רב כהנא said.

keyTerms.meaning: 'your house', from the פסוק about מזוזה
set aside for you, used for living

phrases.english: As it was taught: 'Your house'
means your house that is set aside for you,
to the exclusion of a hay shed and a cattle barn
and a woodshed and storehouses,
which are exempt from mezuza,
and some obligate them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רב כהנא's claim in step 18
steps.raayaObject: Plain barns are subject to a dispute between תנאים
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא on the word 'ביתך' that ends with 'ויש מחייבין'

steps.title: The ברייתא's second list, which both אמוראים must interpret
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: a bathroom, a tannery, a bathhouse, a מקוה, and places where women are 'נאותות' are exempt. Each of the two אמוראים reads this list according to his own view.
steps.simpleTranslation: In truth they said: a bathroom, a tannery, a bathhouse, a מקוה building, and places where women are 'נאותות' are exempt from מזוזה. רב כהנא explains it according to his reasoning, and רב יהודה explains it according to his reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the rest of the ברייתא, which includes the unclear word 'נאותות'. It then announces that both רב כהנא and רב יהודה will explain it their own way, which sets up the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'ושהנשים נאותות בהן' fit neither view automatically, so each אמורא has to show how the ברייתא works for him. This line is a transition: the explanations themselves come next.

keyTerms.meaning: 'in truth they said', introducing an established rule
explains it according to his own reasoning

phrases.english: In truth they said:
a bathroom and a tannery
and a bathhouse and a building for immersion,
and places where women are 'ne'otot'
are exempt from mezuza.
Rav Kahana explains it according to his reasoning,
and Rav Yehuda explains it according to his reasoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא and sets up how each אמורא interprets it
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bathrooms, tanneries, bathhouses, מקוה buildings, and places where women are 'נאותות' are exempt from מזוזה

steps.title: רב כהנא's reading of the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא reads the ברייתא as a dispute only about plain barns, and he explains 'נאותות' as 'bathing'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא explains it his way: 'Your house' means your house set aside for you. This excludes a hay shed, a cattle barn, a woodshed and storehouses, which are exempt from מזוזה when used plainly. And some obligate them when used plainly. In truth they said: a bathroom, a tannery, a bathhouse, a מקוה building, and places where women are 'נאותות'. What is 'נאותות'? Bathing. These are exempt from מזוזה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב כהנא shows how the whole ברייתא fits his view. The dispute is only about plain barns, and 'נאותות' means bathing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By adding the word 'בסתם', רב כהנא limits the argument to ordinary barns. A barn where women bathe is exempt according to everyone, because it fits his definition of 'נאותות' as 'רוחצות'. That bathing place is then listed together with the other dirty places that are exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: in the plain case, with no special use
'make use of'; here explained as bathing

phrases.english: Rav Kahana explains it according to his reasoning:
'Your house' means your house set aside for you,
to the exclusion of a hay shed and a cattle barn
and a woodshed and storehouses,
which are exempt from mezuza in the plain case.
And some obligate them in the plain case.
In truth they said:
a bathroom and a tannery
and a bathhouse and a building for immersion
and places where women are 'ne'otot'
and what is 'ne'otot'? Bathing,
are exempt from mezuza.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out the first of the two interpretations announced in step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the ברייתא to fit his view by limiting the dispute to plain barns and defining 'נאותות'
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא might seem to contradict רב כהנא
steps.terutzMaskana: The dispute is about plain barns only; a place where women bathe is exempt

steps.title: Isn't a bathing place the same as a bathhouse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב כהנא: if 'נאותות' means bathing, the ברייתא repeats itself, because it already listed a bathhouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, it is the same as a bathhouse!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב כהנא's reading. The list would then mention the same thing twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ברייתא does not normally list the same item twice. Since 'bathhouse' is already listed, a separate 'place where women bathe' seems unnecessary, which suggests that 'bathing' is the wrong meaning.

phrases.english: If so, it is the same as a bathhouse!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב כהנא's explanation in step 21
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That definition makes the ברייתא list the same thing twice

steps.title: Teaching both a public and a private bathhouse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'bathhouse' means a public one, and the place where women bathe is a private one. Both had to be stated.
steps.simpleTranslation: It teaches us about a public bathhouse, and it teaches us about a private bathhouse. Because you might have thought: a public bathhouse is exempt, since it has a lot of filth. But a private bathhouse, which does not have a lot of filth, I might say needs a מזוזה. So the ברייתא teaches us that it is also exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב כהנא by showing that the two items are different. One is a public bathhouse, and the other is a private bathing place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without the extra item, we might have thought only a public bathhouse is exempt, because it is very dirty. A private bathhouse is cleaner, so we might have required a מזוזה there. The ברייתא lists both to teach that even a private bathhouse is exempt.

keyTerms.meaning: of the public / of an individual

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב כהנא, 'נאותות' means bathing. The extra mention teaches that even a private, less dirty bathhouse is exempt from מזוזה.

phrases.english: It teaches us about a public bathhouse
and it teaches us about a private bathhouse.
For it could enter your mind to say:
a public bathhouse, whose filth is great, is exempt,
but a private bathhouse,
whose filth is not great,
I would say it is obligated in mezuza;
so it teaches us that it is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 22
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: public versus private bathhouse
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A private bathhouse, being less dirty, needs a מזוזה
steps.terutzMaskana: Both public and private bathhouses are exempt from מזוזה

steps.title: רב יהודה reads the ברייתא according to his own view
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains the ברייתא this way. Plain barns and storehouses are exempt according to all. The dispute is only when women adorn themselves there. So 'נאותות' means 'adorning', not 'bathing'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יהודה explains the ברייתא according to his reasoning. This is what it teaches: 'Your house' means your house that is set aside for you to live in. That excludes a hay storehouse, a cattle barn, a woodshed and a storehouse, which are exempt from מזוזה even if women adorn themselves there. Some obligate them when women adorn themselves there. But in a plain case, everyone agrees they are exempt. In truth they said: a bathroom, a tannery, a bathhouse and a מקוה are exempt from מזוזה even though women adorn themselves there, because they are very dirty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now shows how רב יהודה reads the same ברייתא in a way that fits his opinion, just as it did earlier for רב כהנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב יהודה, the line 'some obligate' is limited to barns where women adorn themselves. A plain barn is exempt according to everyone. This lets him read 'נאותות' as 'adorning', so the last part of the ברייתא says that dirty places stay exempt even when women adorn themselves there.

keyTerms.meaning: Explains the text according to his own reasoning
Women adorn or beautify themselves there, which gives the place a more home-like use
A plain, ordinary case with no special use
'In truth they said', a phrase that introduces a firm, accepted rule

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two readings. For רב כהנא, the dispute is about plain barns. For רב יהודה, plain barns are exempt according to everyone, and the dispute is only when women adorn themselves there.

phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda explains it according to his reasoning:
This is what it teaches:
"Your house" means your house that is set aside for you,
excluding a hay storehouse and a cattle barn
and a woodshed and a storehouse,
which are exempt from mezuza
even when women adorn themselves there.
And some obligate them when women adorn themselves there.
But in a plain case, everyone agrees it is exempt.
phrases.notes: This is the key point of רב יהודה's view.

phrases.english: In truth they said:
a bathroom and a tannery
and a bathhouse and a place of ritual immersion,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁהַנָּשִׁים מִתְקַשְּׁטוֹת בָּהֶן
phrases.english: even though women adorn themselves in them,
are exempt from mezuza,
because their filth is great.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יְהוּדָה מְתָרֵץ לְטַעְמֵיהּ, הָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second אמורא's reading of the same ברייתא, alongside רב כהנא's reading from steps 21 and 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting the ברייתא to fit the אמורא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might have thought the ברייתא only fits רב כהנא's view.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא also fits רב יהודה if the dispute is limited to places where women adorn themselves and 'נאותות' means adorning.

steps.title: Challenge to רב יהודה: a ברייתא obligates barns and storehouses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: does רב יהודה really hold that plain barns are exempt according to everyone? A ברייתא learns from ״בשעריך״ that barns, chicken coops and storehouses are obligated in מזוזה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to רב יהודה, is a plain case exempt according to everyone? But it was taught in a ברייתא: 'Upon your gates' includes the gates of houses, the gates of courtyards, the gates of cities and the gates of towns. Also a barn, chicken coops, a hay storehouse, wine storehouses and oil storehouses are obligated in מזוזה. I might have thought that I include even...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יהודה with a ברייתא that seems to contradict him. The ברייתא keeps going into the next passage with 'I might have thought...'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה said nobody obligates a plain barn or storehouse. This ברייתא lists a barn, a hay storehouse and wine and oil storehouses as obligated, and it says nothing about women adorning themselves there. So it looks like at least one תנא obligates them even in a plain case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But was it not taught in a ברייתא?', which introduces a contradicting source
'Upon your gates', from the פסוק of מזוזה
'I might have thought that I include', which sets up a limit that comes next

steps.whyThisMatters: If this challenge holds, רב יהודה's claim that everyone exempts a plain barn is in trouble. The answer will come on the next amud.

phrases.english: And according to Rav Yehuda,
is a plain case exempt according to everyone?
But was it not taught: "Upon your gates"

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד שַׁעֲרֵי בָתִּים וְאֶחָד שַׁעֲרֵי חֲצֵירוֹת
phrases.english: includes both the gates of houses and the gates of courtyards

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶחָד שַׁעֲרֵי מְדִינוֹת וְאֶחָד שַׁעֲרֵי עֲיָירוֹת,
phrases.english: and the gates of cities and the gates of towns,
and a barn, chicken coops and a hay storehouse
and wine storehouses and oil storehouses
are obligated in mezuza.
phrases.notes: This directly contradicts רב יהודה's view that plain storehouses are exempt according to everyone.

phrases.english: I might have thought that I include even...
phrases.notes: The ברייתא continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְרַב יְהוּדָה סְתָמָא דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל פָּטוּר, וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading רב יהודה just gave in step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's claim that a plain barn or storehouse is exempt according to everyone.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא openly obligates barns and storehouses in מזוזה without mentioning women adorning themselves. That suggests some obligate them even in a plain case.
